title: fix(spec): the dateRange refusal names an empty bound instead of repeating the author's own shape
body:
Fixes #18278

Clause-②: no

`describeRefusedDateRange` in `packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts` described every two-element array as *"a two-element array"*, on an inline comment that stated why nothing else could arrive:

> Two bounds is the arity the contract asks for, so the only way such an
> array reaches a refusal is a bound that is not a string.

That sentence is the one this PR removes, because it was false the whole time the residue it denies was arriving.

## The falsification leg, re-measured first-hand before any edit

`AnalyticsDateRangeSchema`'s array arm is `z.tuple([z.string(), z.string()])`: it judges arity and bound TYPE, never a bound's VALUE. So `['', '']` is **accepted** at every schema door and refused PAST it, by each face's own empty-bound check (`service-analytics/src/date-range-array-arm.ts` line 124, `driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts` line 793) — exactly the residue `analyticsDateRangeUnrecognizedError`'s header in `@objectstack/core` already names as `['', '']`.

Measured on `origin/main` at `ObjectQLStrategy.dateRangeBounds`, with a same-subject control that HITS so a null result could not be a dead probe:

| leg | input | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PROBE | `['', '']` | `THREW ANALYTICS_DATE_RANGE_UNRECOGNIZED / 400` — `… received a two-element array. Refused past the schema door …` |
| CONTROL (live) | `['2026-01-01', '2026-01-31']` | `RETURNED ["2026-01-01","2026-01-31"]` — the face is not refusing everything |
| CONTROL (informative) | `['2026-01-01']` | `… received a 1-element array, not the two bounds [start, end].` |

⇒ the card's claim holds at the face: the author of `['', '']` was handed back the arity they had just written, on a path where the value is never echoed, with nothing said about what was wrong with it. The quoted comment was re-derived from the file rather than taken from the card.

## The fix

- **An empty bound is named, at the bound that is empty** — `['', '']` → `a two-element array whose bounds are both empty strings`; `['', b]` / `[a, '']` → `whose start bound is an empty string` / `whose end bound is an empty string`. Since the sentence never echoes the value on this path, *which* bound is a clause only this builder can supply.
- **A non-string bound keeps its TYPE description.** `['', 3]` still reads `an array with a non-string bound`: the fault the arm itself refuses is named first. The arity descriptions (`[]`, `['a']`, `[a, b, c]`) are byte-identical.
- **`a two-element array` survives as the LIT control** — the description for a two-bound window with nothing this clause can name, refused for something it cannot see (an unparseable bound VALUE keeps its own `DATASET_INVALID` envelope). The empty-bound clause is not claimed when it is not true.
- **The comment is corrected in the same edit**, since a false explanation is what kept the case unexamined. Today it states the mechanism instead: the arm judges TYPE and never VALUE, so the two ways such an array reaches a refusal are a non-string bound and an empty-string bound.

⛔ **The accept set does not move.** `AnalyticsDateRangeSchema.safeParse(['', ''])` still succeeds, and the new spec test asserts that success as the premise of the whole card rather than assuming it.

## Tests — lit control and dark control, and an ablation that proved they can fail

Evidence below was taken at tree `ff9d8e8f33` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `51959b29e5`; the only later commit rewrote a trailer, same tree).

- `packages/spec/src/data/analytics-date-range-two-bound-window.test.ts` — the builder: the empty-bound sentences, the LIT control (`['2026-01-01','2026-01-31']` still reads `received a two-element array.`), the DARK control (`not.toContain('received a two-element array.')` for `['', '']`), the TYPE-before-VALUE ordering, and the accept-set premise.
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/date-range-array-arm-arity.test.ts` — the face an author actually reaches: `['', '']` joins `NOT_A_WINDOW`, so every one of the four faces is now driven over it (envelope identity + byte-for-byte shared wording), plus a focused case on the sentence itself.

| run | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | 494 files / 14521 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics test` | 112 files / 2408 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck && … service-analytics typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `@objectstack/core` `analytics-date-range.test.ts` | 45 passed |
| `driver-memory` date-range array-arity + conformance | 10 passed |
| `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config -f json` | 6877 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings — the whole repo-level population, so no narrowing is claimed |
| derived gate families (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran`) | 83 derived, **79 run green**, 4 NOT MEASURED (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` — each exits 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET without a whole-monorepo build; CI builds it) |

**Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` + `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`, both legs, restore proved by blob hash): with the two empty-bound arms removed from the committed source, the source-resolved spec suite went `1 failed | 12 passed` and — after rebuilding `@objectstack/spec` and preflighting the marker ABSENT from all 214 built files — the dist-resolved face suite went `1 failed | 27 passed`. Restored: blob `b92bd69179a1` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, whole-tree `git status --porcelain` clean, dist rebuilt with the marker present in 22 files, both suites back to 13 / 28 passed.

## Acceptance notes

- **`driver-memory`'s own wording is false for this same input, and is NOT fixed here.** `memory-analytics.ts` refuses `['', '']` with `has a bound that is not a date string (string)` — its own third wording, which #18277 (open, `pm:on-hold`, `domain:engine`) already exists to retire by adopting the shared sentence. Adopting it is what makes that face inherit this repair; `packages/drivers/**` is outside this card's surface, and a sweep from a card that does not own the package is how a shared convention gets moved sideways. Instrument radius: read while confirming the card's "every face also refuses an EMPTY string bound" claim — which holds; both faces check `bound.length === 0`.
- **A whitespace-only bound (`[' ', ' ']`) is not refused by any face** and is therefore not described here either: the description matches the faces' predicate (`length === 0`) exactly, rather than claiming a fault nothing enforces.
- Dedupe was run before any code: no duplicate. Reading and its control are in the report on the card.
